section_summary.extract_value: This section outlines the analytical strategy, beginning with zero-order correlations to examine associations between six executive function measures, ATTA fluency and originality, creative achievements (arts, science, total), and cognitive abilities. Subsequently, two logistic linear regressions were conducted to assess the effect of overall EF and specific EFs (Updating, Shifting, Inhibition) on IT and artistic professional domains. Simple linear regressions were then used to predict self-reported artistic, scientific, and total creative achievements, and to determine if overall EF or unique variance in specific EFs predicted divergent thinking fluency or originality. All analyses were controlled for general cognitive ability, education level, age, and gender. The section defines ATTA, CAQ, and ICAR, and provides Cohen's d effect size interpretations.

section_summary.extract_value: This section outlines the analytical strategy employed, which involved performing zero-order correlations to examine associations between executive functions, creative achievements (measured by ATTA fluency, ATTA originality, and CAQ for arts, science, and total achievements), and cognitive abilities (ICAR). Additionally, logistic and simple linear regressions were conducted to predict professional domains and creative achievements, with all analyses controlling for general cognitive ability, education level, age, and gender. Table 1 provides descriptive statistics and independent group t-tests comparing 'IT' and 'Artistic' professions, including mean ages of 33.00 and 29.79 respectively, and data for ICAR and CAQ measures.
